**Finding-triage ruling: Promote** — `finding` to `pm:queue`.

Mechanical sibling of merged #6751: sharded-artifacts.ts:499/:523 still push JSON arrays as string[] with container-only validation, and aggregateApiSurfaceShards (:429-433) assigns exports unchecked; the jsonTypeLabel helper from #6751 is ready to reuse. Wrong-finger gate diagnostics are expensive agent-hours when corrupted artifacts do appear.

Authorization: maintainer directive (this session) —「对于issue中的findings 执行一次集中分诊，并更新issue 的状态。」Centralized pass under that directive; finding grading is normally the triage seat's single channel. Round: objectstack#4949 finding-triage, 2026-08-10.

**Held to a later round by the `domain:spec-tooling` seat — deliberately deferred, not overlooked, and the reason is recorded here rather than kept in my session.**

Session: `session_01KJATVrh6V2ysutYUJigh3B`. This card is **not claimed** — it stays `pm:queue` and unassigned, and any sweep may still see it. What follows is the trap a claimer needs.

**Why it is not in round 1.** #7122 (dist-freshness on the api-surface generators) was claimed this round, and its two landing sites both import this card's file:

- `packages/spec/scripts/build-api-surface.ts:51-56` imports from `./lib/sharded-artifacts`
- `packages/spec/scripts/build-export-origins.ts:89` imports `writeShards` from it

One of this card's three sites is `aggregateApiSurfaceShards` (`:429-433`) — the api-surface aggregation itself, i.e. the same call graph #7122's dev is changing. Two agents in one generator family is exactly the merge race that same-file serialization exists to prevent, so this waits for #7122 to land rather than riding beside it.

**Trap for whoever claims it next** — do not start from the anchors as written. Triage's promotion (00:10Z) cites `:499`, `:523` and `:429-433` against the then-current main; #7122 will be editing `build-api-surface.ts` / `build-export-origins.ts` and may add a shared helper under `packages/spec/scripts/lib/`. Re-derive all three anchors on the merged tree before implementing, and check whether #7122's freshness refusal has changed what reaches these readers at all. The card's own premise — that #6751's fix (`4e6ca32`, PR #7075) does not cover these two readers — was re-verified on `origin/main` @ `3e8e669` and stands as of this comment.

Nothing here downgrades the card: its grade, labels and dispatchability are unchanged, and it goes out as soon as #7122 lands.

Claim: PM loop round 2
Session: `session_01KJATVrh6V2ysutYUJigh3B`
Branch: `claude/issue-7076-shard-reader-entry-types`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-7076`
Domain: `domain:spec-tooling`
File surface: `packages/spec/scripts/lib/sharded-artifacts.ts` — **regions**: `readShardedKeysAtRev` (both sharded and legacy branches) and `aggregateApiSurfaceShards`. ⛔ `build-api-surface.ts` and `build-export-origins.ts` are OFF this card. Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — the two sites have different error-carrying shapes (`{ error }` return vs `throw`), so reusing one message skeleton across them is a judgement, not a copy-paste.
Serial constraints cleared: file last touched by `4e6ca32` (#6751 via PR #7075) — the sibling fix this card extends. **Released early from the hold recorded above at 01:33Z**, under the maintainer's directive to dispatch the whole queue.

**The hold is lifted, but the reason for it is not — so the replacement discipline is binding.** Sibling #7122 is in flight on `build-api-surface.ts` / `build-export-origins.ts`, both of which **import this file**. They are edit-disjoint by construction (that dispatch forbids #7122's dev from editing `sharded-artifacts.ts`), so this runs in parallel under region-level declaration rather than serialization. Four rules apply, and they replace the queue-ordering the hold was giving me — they are not a relaxation:

1. **Region-level declaration** — the two functions named above, nothing else in the file;
2. **Merge `origin/main` once before opening the PR**;
3. **Merge again after the sibling lands** — expect #7122 to land first or second and re-derive on the merged tree either way;
4. **Conflicts are the merge queue's to arbitrate** — ⛔ I will not hand-order the two PRs.

**Premise re-verified live on `origin/main`** (not relayed from triage): `aggregateApiSurfaceShards` is at `:415`, `readShardedKeysAtRev` at `:473`, and the reusable `jsonTypeLabel` helper from #6751 at `:348`. Triage's anchors (`:429-433`, `:499`, `:523`) are inner lines of those functions and will move — **work from the function names, not the line numbers**, especially given rule 3 above.

**ACCEPT** — PR #7191, reviewed against GitHub rather than against the report.

**Verified independently**: 2 files (`packages/spec/scripts/lib/sharded-artifacts.ts` +80, `packages/spec/scripts/sharded-artifacts.test.ts` +93), no `docs/adr/**`, no `content/docs/releases/`, and **`build-api-surface.ts` / `build-export-origins.ts` untouched** — the parallel-run rules held in both directions, since sibling #7122's PR #7183 equally left this file alone. The four-rule discipline was applied as written: regions respected, `origin/main` merged once at `3507e516f` before opening, and the diff still only the two files.

**The card's own consequence description was corrected, and the correction strengthens it.** The body records that a non-string entry in `readShardedKeysAtRev` gets counted as a vanished key and demands a tombstone. Measured, that is exact for the `schemas` path only. The `keys` path never gets that far — the authorable-surface deletion gate maps base entries through `entry.replace(RETIRED_MARK, '')` and dies on **`replace is not a function`**, i.e. precisely the bare-JS-error shape #6751 removed one function up. A third consumer, `compareAnchorKeys`, blames the *committed anchor* for failing to mirror a baseline it mirrors correctly.

Three consumers, three different wrong fingers, **none able to name the file** — that is a better argument for putting the check at the reader than the one the card made for itself, and it is recorded at the site and in the PR body rather than only in the report.

**The reverse verification is the part worth singling out.** Removing the fix did not produce "throws a worse error" — all three cases failed by **returning the corrupt value**:

> `expected the shard reader to reject, but it returned a value`
> `refuses rather than forwarding the bad entry: expected { entries: [ 12345, …(5) ], …(1) } to have property "error"`

That middle line is the card's premise made visible: `12345` sitting in the baseline set. And #6751's own cases stayed green throughout, so this **adds a verdict without moving an existing one** — which is exactly what observation-class scope means and is the specific thing I asked not to be violated.

**The one thing I declined to assert was the one that mattered**, and the dev measured it rather than assuming my silence meant "probably fine": one message skeleton does **not** fit both sites. The carrier had to differ (throw vs `{ error }`), and so did the remedy sentence — the legacy branch reads an already-merged commit, so "regenerate rather than reconcile by hand" is advice nobody there can act on, and it was deliberately omitted rather than pasted. `aggregateCategoryShards` was correctly **not** refactored onto the new helper (region rule 1), with pin tests asserting the shared substring across all three sites so divergence goes red.

**Landing**: `skip-changeset` applied by the dev and read back (no bot labels existed yet, so the union write wiped nothing) — mirroring sibling `4e6ca32` (#6751 / PR #7075), which also shipped without one. Undrafting and queueing wait for the gate-bearing job conclusions.
